item.title: ⚠️ APACHE CXF TOKEN-VALIDATION FLAWS CAN ENABLE USER IMPERSONATION Apache disclosed two "important" Apache CXF vulnerabilities on Oct 9, 2026, both ...
item.description:
⚠️ APACHE CXF TOKEN-VALIDATION FLAWS CAN ENABLE USER IMPERSONATION

Apache disclosed two "important" Apache CXF vulnerabilities on Oct 9, 2026, both in how the framework validates security tokens. Fixed releases shipped Oct 8.

What Apache says:
• CVE-2026-97468: the Security Token Service (STS) and STSTokenValidator cached validated tokens under a weak 32-bit hash and treated a cache hit as proof of validity, so a colliding token could bypass credential or signature checks and impersonate another user
• CVE-2026-97791: STSTokenValidator stored its "signed by a trusted certificate" result in one object shared by all requests, so one request could inherit another's trust decision and an untrusted SAML assertion could be accepted
• Affected: CXF 4.2.0 before 4.2.4, 4.0.0 before 4.1.9, and versions before 3.6.13
• Fix: upgrade to 4.2.4, 4.1.9 or 3.6.13

⚠️ Analyst Note:
Apache reports no exploitation in the wild and no public exploit. The SAML race matters for STSTokenValidator setups without alwaysValidateToSts and needs concurrent legitimate traffic. Check both your CXF branch and your token-validation configuration.

Source:
https://openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/10/09/9
https://openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/10/09/10

#DDW #DarkWeb #Vulnerability #ApacheCXF #CyberSecurity #ThreatIntelligence

item.title: 🇮🇳 🇦🇪 🚨 THREAT ACTOR SELLS SMS LOGS TIED TO HEYDUDE INDIA, SALARYBOX, ASTROYOGI AND FRAGRANT SOUQ A single seller on an underground for...
item.description:
🇮🇳 🇦🇪 🚨 THREAT ACTOR SELLS SMS LOGS TIED TO HEYDUDE INDIA, SALARYBOX, ASTROYOGI AND FRAGRANT SOUQ

A single seller on an underground forum has listed four datasets in one afternoon, each presented as a "database" of a well-known brand. The samples point to SMS messaging logs rather than classic user databases.

The listings claim:
* HeyDude India (http://heydude.in): 15M records, names, mobile numbers and cart-reminder texts
* SalaryBox (Indian HR/payroll SaaS): 4M records, renewal and attendance reminder SMS
* Astroyogi (astrology platform): 2.9M records, SMS logs reportedly including one-time passcodes and booking links
* Fragrant Souq (UAE perfume retailer): 110K records, customer names and order-confirmation texts
* Samples show phone numbers, mobile carriers, delivery status and timestamps from mid-2026
* Asking prices between 1K and 3K per set

⚠️ Analyst Note:
The four samples share the same messaging-gateway style log format, which may point to a compromised SMS or customer-messaging provider rather than four separate brand breaches. Phone numbers paired with real order, payroll or booking context make very convincing smishing lures. None of the companies had confirmed an incident at the time of writing, and the data has not been verified.

This is an unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation that any of these companies was breached.
